reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with holidays and adds a shared isHoliday, but the daily-schedule skip rule is not given a shared function and is rewritten at each consumer.

duplication.why: The skipDailyWeekends flag, the weekend/holiday filter and the holiday-sized lookahead are written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and the reverse fallback in getNextDate omits the holiday check.

placement.why: isHoliday and the move logic sit in shared/schedules.ts, but the per-occurrence 'skip or move' decision is spread across server/schedules/app.ts handlers instead of living beside them.

scope.why: Edits are all tied to the four steps (types, rule parsing, helpers, handlers, template), with no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: Any further change to weekend/holiday handling must be repeated in three hand-written pipelines plus schedule-template, which already disagrees on daily schedules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts re-implement the daily skip filter instead of sharing getNextDate's logic; schedule-template.ts calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly and so still moves daily weekend occurrences.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily weekend/holiday skip appears as a post-take filter in getNextDate, a filter+slice with an inflated take in getUpcomingDates, and a widened-window filter in getDatesInRange: the same rule reshaped three times.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter; getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each decide the daily skip themselves, and schedule-template's two calls bypass the daily rule.
